answer: Pin every new identity to a randomly assigned vertex in the incumbent countersigner graph and require a slashable opal bond, locked to one signing key. Reputation can drain only through a karst of underground co-signer channels that have not appeared in any other applicant's path for two epochs. If two identities later share a channel or a key, the graph collapses them into one sink and seizes both bonds. A farm that wants N sockpuppets must therefore buy N distinct unused neighborhoods and N full opal stakes; copying one social graph is a detectable merge, not N votes.
